text:
sam: Heads-up — seeing duplicated SSE chunks when auth refresh and reconnect happen near-simultaneously. Repro in our Node sample app.
anya: ugh. which SDK/version?
sam: node-sdk v0.9.3, streaming helper using EventSource polyfill. Happens when token refresh triggers a reconnect during an in-flight chunk.
matt: any logs? sequence numbers?
sam: pasted snippet from the client logs: 
```
[stream] recv chunk id=abc123 seq=87
[stream] auth refresh start
[stream] connection closed by client
[stream] reconnect resume_token=tok_xyz
[stream] recv chunk id=abc123 seq=86   # out-of-order duplicate, seq went backwards
[stream] recv chunk id=def456 seq=88
```
jess: interesting — seq going backwards means server resumed from an earlier offset, or the client applied resume logic incorrectly. Could be a race between resume_token validity and the server's buffer GC.
anya: does python SDK show same?
sam: tried python edge-client 0.8.1, same pattern but less frequent. Node's auto-reconnect logic seems to immediately replay buffered chunks when `lastEventId` present.
matt: can you share the minimal repro? if it's small we can add an integration test to prevent regressions.
sam: repro steps in repo: `examples/long-stream-reconnect/`. Key bits: force token refresh with `AUTH_EXPIRE_MS=1000`, stream a large response (10k tokens), kill connection during a partial chunk.
jess: idea: add monotonic chunk_seq validation on client that drops any chunk with seq <= last_applied_seq and emits a metric. That would be a pragmatic DX fix while we investigate server resume semantics.
anya: agree. Also we should make Node SDK preserve `lastEventId` -> `resume_token` semantics consistently: if we reconnect and server assigns an older resume point, the client should request a full retransmit or throw a non-retryable error.
matt: open a PR?
sam: opened draft PR #2412 with client-side seq guard + tests. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/node-sdk/pull/2412
infra-bot: deploy queued for branch stream-fix (reviewers: @matt @jess) :rocket:
jess: one more note — sample app onboarding: add `STREAM_DEBUG=true` to env so users can see chunk IDs and seqs in logs. Save a lot of hours for customers.
anya: also add a short section in docs: "When to prefer no-auth-reconnect for long-running streams" and note heuristics.
sam: thanks. I'll update the example and land the seq-guard patch after tests. If folks want to pair on server-side resume semantics, ping me. :thumbsup:
